what.text: Asylum seekers and refugees from Colombia live in several host countries, including Ecuador, Venezuela, Canada, Costa Rica, and the United States.
By the end of 2025, there were 190214 Colombian asylum seekers with pending protection claims in the United States.
At the end of 2025, 5460 refugees from Colombia were residing in the United States under UNHCR's mandate.

why.text: Displacement occurred alongside the Armed conflict over the government of Colombia, which was active from 1995 to 2025.
During the period from 1995 to 2025, the Government of Colombia fought against opposition groups including ELN, FARC, EPL–Los Pelusos, FARC-EMC, FARC - Segunda Marquetalia, and EMBF.

when.text: The count of asylum seekers from Colombia in the United States stood at 2489 at the end of 2000.
The figure for pending asylum claims in the United States reached a peak of 250260 by the end of 2024.
Following that peak, the total number of pending asylum applications in the United States decreased by the end of 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes displaced individuals traveled or where and how they live in host countries.
The figures count asylum seekers from Colombia in the United States as year-end totals of people whose protection claims have not yet been decided.
Refugee numbers record people outside Colombia needing international protection counted under UNHCR's mandate at year end.
